name: thirty rounds of one project with three drifts: the map stays structured (few top-level nodes, one node per topic, the drifts kept apart), the block stays under budget, the focus tracks the work (structure and cost over time)

rounds.user: The venue: the old town hall holds 180 seated; quote is 2,400 for the day.
Town hall AV is weak — we would need to rent a projector and two mics.
rounds.assistant: Venue AV: rent a projector and two microphones.

rounds.user: Speakers: Dana Whitfield has agreed to keynote; 40 minutes plus questions.
Second speaker: Tom Ruiz on community energy — he asked for a morning slot.
rounds.assistant: Speaker: Tom Ruiz, community energy, morning slot requested.

rounds.user: Budget ceiling is 9,000 total; venue and AV must stay under 3,500.
Unrelated — can you remind me what the capital of Mongolia is?
Catering: the vegetarian buffet from Greenleaf, 18 per head, they need numbers a week ahead.
rounds.assistant: Catering: Greenleaf vegetarian buffet, 18/head, headcount one week ahead.

rounds.user: Tickets: 35 standard, 15 student, sold through the usual platform; early bird ends 1 May.
rounds.assistant: Tickets: 35 / 15 student; early bird ends 1 May.

rounds.user: Dana would like her slides reviewed by us two weeks before — put that in the plan.
rounds.assistant: Keynote slides review two weeks before the event.

rounds.user: Decision: we take the town hall despite the AV; rental of AV goes on the budget line.
rounds.assistant: Decided: town hall; AV rental added to budget.

rounds.user: Revised budget: venue 2,400, AV 600, catering 3,240 for 180, speakers travel 800, printing 300, contingency 500.
Also — what year did the town hall get built? Just curious.
Sales after week one: 62 tickets, 40 of them student. Slower than hoped on standard.
We should do a second announcement through the university mailing list and the two local newsletters.
rounds.assistant: Marketing: university list + two local newsletters, second announcement.

rounds.user: Tom Ruiz confirmed for 10:30; he needs a whiteboard, not slides.
Greenleaf can add a gluten-free option for 2 more per head — yes to that.
Volunteers: we need six on the day — two on the door, two for AV, two floating.
Priya and Sam have volunteered; four more to find, ask the student society.
rounds.assistant: Volunteers: Priya, Sam confirmed; four via student society.

rounds.user: Sales week two: 118 total. Standard picked up after the newsletter.
Ticket revenue projection at 160 sold: about 4,100 — so we still need the 3,000 sponsorship.
rounds.assistant: Revenue projection 4,100 at 160 sold; sponsorship 3,000 needed.

rounds.user: Sponsorship: the credit union offered 2,000 for logo placement and a two-minute welcome slot.
rounds.assistant: Sponsor: credit union, 2,000 for logo + 2-min welcome.

rounds.user: We accept the credit union offer. Still 1,000 short — try the bookshop.
rounds.assistant: Accepted credit union; approach the bookshop for 1,000.

rounds.user: Quick one: how do you say thank you in Norwegian?
Draft schedule: doors 9, welcome 9:30, keynote 9:45, Tom 10:30, break 11:15, panel 11:45, lunch 12:45.
Move the break to 11:00 so the panel has a full hour.
Town hall confirmed in writing; deposit of 800 paid.
Final headcount to Greenleaf by 24 May.
Week three: 141 sold. We will likely sell out standard; keep 10 for sponsors.
Ask Dana if we can quote her in the final announcement.
rounds.assistant: Marketing: request a Dana quote for the final announcement.

rounds.user: Final schedule sent to speakers; Tom asked for 10:35 instead of 10:30, granted.
